title: Introduction to Chemistry - Chemistry - Lab Safety
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the correct procedure for mixing a concentrated acid with water?
options: Pour water into the acid quickly.
Pour the acid into the water slowly.
Mix them together in a closed container.
Heat the acid before adding water.
questions.explain: Always add **Acid to Water** (AA - Add Acid). Adding water to acid can cause the water to boil instantly and splash acid due to the large amount of heat released.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which piece of personal protective equipment (PPE) is most critical when working with liquid chemicals?
questions.explain: Safety goggles are essential to protect eyes from chemical splashes. Contact lenses can trap chemicals, and sandals/loose clothing are hazards.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: If you accidentally spill a chemical on your skin, what is the first thing you should generally do?
options: Neutralize it with another chemical immediately.
Wipe it off with a paper towel.
Flush the area with large amounts of water.
Wait to see if it burns.
questions.explain: The immediate response to a skin spill is to flush the area with water (usually for 15 minutes) to dilute and remove the chemical.
